open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin” does not define the cookie's host/domain, path, SameSite policy, persistence or whether local HTTP and remote HTTPS receive different attributes
open_points.question: Which exact cookie attributes and scope enforce the stated browser boundary, particularly because cookies are not scoped by port?
options: Host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, owner-interface path, Secure whenever HTTPS is used
Host-only, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, root path, with Secure selected from the request scheme
Leave the attributes to the implementation
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to the owner-interface path, with Secure required on HTTPS.

open_points.subject: A13 concurrent owner requests
open_points.text: The session's last-request instant and pending confirmation are mutable, but only “Concurrent sign-ins are counted one at a time”; no ordering rule covers concurrent requests in one owner session
open_points.question: How are simultaneous requests in one owner session ordered when they refresh last_request, show competing confirmations, consume a confirmation, sign out, or upload a file?
options: Serialize every mutation of one owner session
Use atomic compare-and-change operations with whichever request commits first winning
Permit last-writer-wins behavior
open_points.default_guess: Serialize mutations per owner session and let each request act on the state left by the preceding committed request.

open_points.subject: A13 sign-out racing an accepted request
open_points.text: “a request that passes [validity] completes even if a limit passes while it runs” mentions time limits but does not say what happens if the same session is signed out while that request is running
open_points.question: May a request that passed the session check commit after a concurrent sign-out?
options: Yes, every request that passed stage 1 completes
No, sign-out invalidates any request not yet committed
Whichever transaction commits first determines the result
open_points.default_guess: Whichever serialized session operation commits first determines whether the other is accepted.

open_points.subject: A15 audit erasure versus restore
open_points.text: A15 says entries are “removed only by 'erase audit entries before a date'” while A18 says restoring a backup replaces the store and loses every audit entry written after the backup
open_points.question: Is restoration an explicit second way the current audit log may lose entries, or is A15 intended to describe only Registry API actions?
options: A15 governs only Registry actions; host restoration may roll the log back
A restore must preserve or merge later audit entries
Restoration is forbidden whenever it would lose audit entries
open_points.default_guess: Treat A15 as an API invariant and document restoration as an external rollback exception.

open_points.subject: A16 mapping of unpicked malformed records
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the mapping shows “every malformed record and every id that conflicts,” but rule 3 says records only of unpicked projects “are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported”
open_points.question: Must malformed records and conflicts belonging solely to unpicked projects be detected and shown?
options: No; validate and show defects only in the selected closure
Yes; show every defect in the file even though only selected projects are imported
Show syntax-level defects globally but semantic defects only for selected projects
open_points.default_guess: Validate and show defects only for the selected projects and the records they bring.

open_points.subject: A16 imported project names
open_points.text: A16 permits a picked project to arrive under “its v1 name and no alias unless the owner gives others,” while R0-82 says projects imported under a person's name are renamed and R0-85 says this happens in the import itself
open_points.question: When must confirmation require a replacement display name instead of accepting the v1 name, and how can Registry determine that the v1 name identifies a person?
options: Require the owner to provide a new display name for every picked project
Allow every v1 name and make renaming solely an unchecked owner obligation
Add a per-project owner assertion that the displayed name satisfies R0-82
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to affirm or replace each displayed name, without attempting to infer whether it names a person.

open_points.subject: A16 upload and confirmation races
open_points.text: Another upload replaces the session's file and a confirmation applies only the retained digest, but no atomic ordering is stated between upload, mapping generation and confirmation in the same session
open_points.question: What result is required when an upload races a confirmation or two uploads race each other?
options: Serialize all import-file operations per owner session
Allow either upload to win, with confirmation accepted only if its digest still matches at commit
Reject concurrent import-file operations
open_points.default_guess: Serialize them per owner session and recheck the retained digest in the confirmation transaction.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup in owner-only mode
open_points.text: A16 requires “Right after an accepted import Registry makes a backup run,” while A18 says “an owner-only start makes no run” and an import can be performed through the owner interface when no service tokens are configured
open_points.question: Does an accepted import trigger its special backup when Registry is running owner-only?
options: Yes; the import backup is an exception to the owner-only prohibition
No; it waits until a later start with service tokens
Import itself is refused in owner-only mode
open_points.default_guess: Run the special post-import backup even in owner-only mode.

open_points.subject: A17 empty store location
open_points.text: “An empty store location is made into a new, empty store” does not define whether empty means a missing path, an empty directory, a zero-length file, or an empty configuration value
open_points.question: Exactly which filesystem states authorize Registry to create a new store, and which must fail startup?
options: Only a configured path that does not yet exist may be created
A missing path or an empty directory may be initialized
A missing, zero-length or otherwise empty target may be initialized
open_points.default_guess: Create a store only when the configured target does not exist; refuse existing unreadable, zero-length or unrecognized targets.

open_points.subject: A17 secret length and equality
open_points.text: Secrets must be “at least 32 bytes long” and unequal, but the text does not define the byte representation of configured textual credentials
open_points.question: Which decoding or encoding is used to measure secret length, compare equality and obtain the bytes used for authentication and encryption?
options: Configuration supplies encoded binary values with one declared decoding
Measure the UTF-8 bytes of the configured text
Treat 32 characters as equivalent to 32 bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require one declared binary encoding and apply length and equality checks to the decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” does not specify an authenticated-encryption construction, nonce generation, key interpretation, metadata authentication or file format
open_points.question: What exact cryptographic format must implementations use so that independently written backup and restore code are compatible and tampering is detected?
options: Declare one versioned authenticated-encryption format and nonce rule
Use the store engine's encrypted-backup facility if available
Let each implementation choose its own encrypted format
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption format with a fresh random nonce and authenticated metadata.

open_points.subject: A18 key digest
open_points.text: A backup records “a digest of the key it was made with” but no digest algorithm, encoding, truncation or domain separation is declared
open_points.question: How is the backup-key identifier computed and compared?
options: A fixed cryptographic hash of the raw decoded key
A keyed or domain-separated identifier derived from the key
An implementation-defined digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed, domain-separated cryptographic hash of the decoded key and store its full canonical encoding.

open_points.subject: A18 audit-sequence backup check
open_points.text: The backup records “the last audit sequence number it holds” and checking requires that “its audit log ends at the recorded sequence number,” while A15 keeps a separate last-ever sequence counter even when the corresponding entries have been erased
open_points.question: Does the metadata and integrity check use the store's last-ever sequence counter or the highest surviving audit entry, and how is an empty audit log checked?
options: Record and verify the separate last-ever counter
Record and verify the highest surviving entry, with a distinct empty value
Record both values and verify both
open_points.default_guess: Record both the last-ever counter and the highest surviving entry, and verify each explicitly.

open_points.subject: A18 recovery-point guarantee
open_points.text: Rule 7 says “a restore loses at most a day of changes” while rule 9 permits the owner to restore “a backup,” including backups retained for up to 30 days
open_points.question: Must restoration use the newest successfully checked backup, or may the owner choose an older retained backup and lose more than a day?
options: Only the newest usable checked backup may be restored
Any retained backup may be restored; the one-day statement is only about backup frequency
An older backup may be restored only when every newer backup is unusable
open_points.default_guess: Use the newest usable checked backup; allow an older one only when newer backups cannot be restored, and qualify the loss guarantee accordingly.

open_points.subject: A18 retention reconciliation after restore
open_points.text: The owner must reconcile restored Customers, projects and audit erasures “before configuring the tokens,” but Registry “cannot list them, enforce them or tell when this is done”
open_points.question: What prevents service access from being enabled before the required post-restore privacy reconciliation is complete?
options: Nothing technical; this is solely an administrative procedure
Persist a recovery-pending gate that only an explicit owner completion action clears
Require creation of a new configuration or store marker after reconciliation
open_points.default_guess: Add a durable recovery-pending gate that refuses service tokens until the owner explicitly completes reconciliation.

open_points.subject: A01 replay equality for structured facts
open_points.text: A repeat requires supplied facts to equal the record's current facts, but A02 defines comparison only for blank and written string values; project object characteristics and other State 6 values may be structured
open_points.question: What equality relation decides replay for objects, collections, numbers and other structured create inputs?
options: Equality of their parsed canonical domain values
Byte-for-byte equality of the submitted representation
Field-specific equality declared with each State 6 schema
open_points.default_guess: Compare parsed canonical domain values using equality declared by the State 6 schema.

open_points.subject: A01 replay after correction and restoration
open_points.text: Rule 4 accepts when supplied facts equal the record's “current facts,” while rule 5 includes “or the record corrected since” as a reason to refuse; a record can be corrected away from its creation facts and later corrected back, and no original-facts snapshot is retained
open_points.question: Is a replay accepted when the current editable facts again equal the original create request after intervening corrections?
options: Yes; only current-fact equality matters
No; any accepted correction permanently prevents create replay
No only while the revision differs from the creation revision, which must be retained
open_points.default_guess: Use current-fact equality, since the model retains neither the original facts nor a creation revision snapshot.

open_points.subject: A01 request-id removal on erasure
open_points.text: A01 says a request id leaves with erased or anonymised values and “a create arriving after that with the same request id is a new create,” while R0-36 says a create repeated after a lost answer “never silently makes a second project, customer or room”
open_points.question: Does replay protection survive project anonymisation, project deletion and Customer erasure, or may the same request id create a replacement record afterward?
options: Keep a non-personal replay tombstone so the request id remains consumed
Allow reuse after erasure as A01 states
Allow reuse only after whole project deletion, not anonymisation or Customer erasure
open_points.default_guess: Keep a minimal non-personal request-id tombstone so a retry cannot create another record.

open_points.subject: A04 project-set check stage
open_points.text: Rule 6 places “the session and its set” in stage (2), but also lists “not in the set” among stage (6) lifecycle checks
open_points.question: At which stage is membership in the agent session's granted set checked?
options: Only stage 2, before existence and value checks
Only stage 6, after revision checks
Stage 2 for authorization and stage 6 only for a distinct post-check that must be defined
open_points.default_guess: Check membership only at stage 2 so its not-found refusal hides every later failure.

open_points.subject: restored audit sequence numbers
open_points.text: M09 says sequence numbers are “never reused in that store” but also says a restored store “continues from the backup's last number”; numbers assigned after that backup can therefore be assigned again after restoration
open_points.question: Does sequence-number uniqueness cover the store's full pre-restore history, or only the restored lineage now present?
options: Only the restored lineage; historical numbers lost by rollback may be reused
The full store history; restoration must retain a high-water mark outside the backup
Add a restore generation to audit identity so repeated numeric sequences remain distinct
open_points.default_guess: Persist a high-water mark outside ordinary backups or add a restore generation so an audit-entry identity is never reused.

open_points.subject: existence of audit entries lost on restore
open_points.text: M09 says entries written after the restored backup “are lost with it and exist nowhere,” but A18 retains other backups for 30 days and a newer retained backup may still contain those entries
open_points.question: Are post-backup entries required to be destroyed from every newer backup during restoration, or does “exist nowhere” mean only that they are absent from the restored live store?
options: They may remain in newer encrypted backups; only the live store loses them
Every newer backup must be deleted when an older backup is restored
Restoring an older backup is allowed only when no newer backup exists
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the statement as absence from the restored live store; retained backups may still contain the entries until normal deletion.

open_points.subject: migration closure across restore
open_points.text: M10 says no backup made before the import “is ever restored,” but restoration is an owner action outside Registry and A18 provides no enforceable refusal mechanism
open_points.question: How is restoration of a pre-import backup prevented or detected so that the one-time import cannot reopen?
options: It is only an administrative promise
Backup tooling refuses a backup that lacks the migration closure once import has occurred
A durable external import marker survives store restoration and is checked at startup
open_points.default_guess: Keep a durable import-completed marker outside the replaceable store and refuse startup from a backup that lacks the closure.

open_points.subject: owner-session import files after another session imports
open_points.text: M11 says an uploaded import file is “dropped when the import is accepted,” while A16 says that after one session accepts the import “a file another session keeps stays until that session ends”
open_points.question: When any session accepts the one import, are uploaded files in all other owner sessions dropped immediately or retained until those sessions end?
options: Drop every session's uploaded import file when the closure is committed
Drop only the confirming session's file and retain the others
End every owner session after import
open_points.default_guess: Drop every retained import file when the migration closure is committed, because none can be used afterward and each contains personal data.
